title: Security questionnaire — executive snapshot for RBAC v2, audit logs, SIEM export
body:
Purpose and audience:
This is an internal one-page draft intended for two audiences: (1) product/security owners who will assemble answers to customer security questionnaires and (2) solutions/CS teams who need a compact evidence map to send to a customer. The doc synthesizes how RBAC v2, the audit log schema, SIEM export formats, and our evidence automation pieces map to common questionnaire asks.

Executive summary (elevator):
- RBAC v2: attribute-aware, least-privilege-first role model with scoped roles, separation-of-duties controls, and audit-friendly role-change history. Supports SCIM and SAML for provisioning; API-first role exports for evidence.
- Audit logs: single canonical event schema (JSON) with standardized fields for actor, actor_type, principal_id, request_id, trace_id, action, resource, resource_type, outcome, timestamp, source_ip, user_agent, and policy_version. Logs are append-only, signed, and stored to an immutable store for N days based on tier.
- SIEM export: native JSON plus CEF adapter. Exports are push (webhook) and pull (S3/forwarder) modes; support for common vendors (Splunk, Sumo Logic, Datadog, Elastic) and configurable field mapping.
- Evidence automation: questionnaire -> artifact mappings in a small rules engine. Where available we attach automated artifacts (role-export, policy diff, filtered audit extract) and mark remaining items for human review.

Typical questionnaire items and our canonical response/artifact mapping (compact):
- Q: Describe roles and how least-privilege is enforced.
  Answer: RBAC v2 implements role templates with parameterized resource scopes (org/project/model). We enforce least-privilege via role inheritance checks and a predeploy policy linter that rejects overly broad grants.
  Evidence: role-definition-export (CSV/JSON), role-template docs (Confluence), policy-linter report (automated).

- Q: How are role changes logged and reviewed?
  Answer: All role lifecycle events (create/update/delete/assign/revoke) are emitted to the audit log with previous/new snapshots, actor id, and request_id. Critical role changes (admin roles) trigger automated approval workflows and MFA gating in the console.
  Evidence: filtered audit extract (last 90 days), role-change webhook delivery logs, approval workflow runbook (Confluence).

- Q: Can we receive audit logs in our SIEM?
  Answer: Yes. Two supported modes: (1) continuous push via HTTPS (JSON/CEF) to a customer endpoint or partner forwarder; (2) periodic archival export to S3 for customer ingestion. Data and field mappings are configurable per-customer.
  Evidence: sample SIEM payload (JSON + CEF), export-config screenshot, published field mapping table (Confluence).

- Q: How do you ensure integrity and retention of logs?
  Answer: Logs are written to an append-only, WORM-backed bucket with server-side signing/validation. Retention is policy-driven (default 90 days for hosted customers; configurable for enterprise). Chain-of-custody metadata (ingest_ts, stored_by, checksum) is retained alongside artifacts.
  Evidence: storage policy doc, sample checksum manifest, retention configuration screenshot.

Audit log schema highlights (quick reference):
- event_id: string (uuid)
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- actor.id / actor.type (user/service/principal)
- principal_id (customer-specific unique id for tenant-scoped events)
- request_id / trace_id
- action (namespace::verb e.g., roles.assign)
- resource.id / resource.type / resource_path (hierarchical)
- outcome (success/failure/denied)
- policy_version (if a policy evaluated)
- source.ip / user_agent
- meta: {session_id, region, replica_info} (JSON blob)
Retention/partitioning notes: daily partitions, compressed JSONL, SHA256 manifest per-partition. We retain manifests for auditability even where logs are purged.

SIEM export details (operational):
- Formats supported: JSONL (canonical), CEF (for legacy SIEMs).
- Delivery: HTTPS push with mutual TLS option; S3 drop with signed temporary credentials; syslog-forwarder via partner connector.
- Field mapping: we publish a default mapping, but customers can provide a mapping file. We maintain a mapping registry per-customer to keep runbooks and parsers in sync.
- Filtering: exports can be filtered by event severity, resource type, or time window to limit egress costs and sensitive fields.

Evidence automation status matrix (what we can attach automatically vs manual):
- role-definition-export (JSON): auto (api endpoint, available)
- filtered audit extract (time-windowed): semi-auto (requires query parameters + human review for sensitive events)
- SIEM sample payload: auto (template + per-customer mapping generation)
- policy linter report: auto (on PR/deploy)
- architecture diagram + data-flow: manual (templated doc that requires confirmation)
- attestation letter / SOC-like statements: manual (legal/security collab)

Common customer redline asks and our mitigation language (short):
- "Can we get raw PII logs?" -> We do not export raw PII. We offer filtered exports and can perform on-demand redaction or hashes as part of an approved support engagement.
- "Longer retention" -> Supported on enterprise contracts; provide signed addendum and separate storage pricing.
- "Cross-tenant visibility" -> Not permitted; we validate principal_id and tenant context on export endpoints.

Operational runbook pointers (where to find/what to run):
- For a typical questionnaire (30–60 mins triage): 1) run role-export for affected scope, 2) generate a 90-day filtered audit extract for key actions, 3) produce SIEM sample payload and field mapping. Use the automation tool: /tools/evidence-assembler (internal).
- Escalation: If the filtered extract contains >1K high-severity events, tag SEC-URG and notify on #sec-answers for triage.

Open items and decisions needed (action owner in parentheses):
- Decide on default retention tiers and published public table (Product -> finalize by 2026-03-20) (Marco Alvarez).
- Approve canned wording for "PII export" fallback for CS responses (Legal + Security) (Jing Wei to loop in Legal).
- Finalize the sample SIEM CEF field mapping for Splunk (SRE + Integrations) (Olivia Chen).
- Automate generation of role-change diffs in the evidence assembler (Engineering ETA: Q2 2026) (Samir Patel).

Quick checklist for CS to assemble files for customer delivery:
- [ ] Role export (JSON) for requested scope
- [ ] Policy linter report for the last deployment
- [ ] Filtered audit extract (CSV/JSONL) covering requested time window
- [ ] SIEM sample payload + mapping table
- [ ] Data flow diagram (templated)
- [ ] Support/contract note on retention and pricing (if relevant)

Notes to self / talking points for customer calls:
- Emphasize policy_version and request_id: we can correlate actions across services for a full chain-of-custody.
- Offer to run a short "evidence pack" proof: 24–48 hour turnaround for standard scope (role export + 30-day audit slice + SIEM sample).
- Keep canned FAQ versions for common questionnaire items to speed responses.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-05 created by Priya Sinha (initial skeleton + mapping)
- 2026-03-10 updated with automation status and open item owners

Appendix: example short excerpt for customer reply (copy-paste friendly):
"Redwood implements RBAC v2 with parameterized role templates to enforce least privilege. All role lifecycle events and authorization decisions are recorded in a canonical audit log (event schema available on request). Customers can ingest logs to their SIEM via secure push or periodic archival exports; we support JSON and CEF formats and provide a per-customer field mapping. Where available, we will attach automated artifacts (role exports, policy linter reports, filtered audit extracts). For PII-related exports we require an approved request and will apply redaction/hashing as per our data handling policy. If you need a sample evidence pack, we can prepare one in 24–48 hours."

End of snapshot.
